entries.claim: Bayes' theorem gives the posterior as proportional to the likelihood times the prior, P(theta|D) proportional to P(D|theta) P(theta)
entries.locator: Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, Chapter 1

entries.claim: With a Beta(alpha,beta) prior and binomial data of h successes in n trials, the posterior is Beta(alpha+h, beta+n-h), a conjugate update
A Bayesian credible interval admits the statement that the parameter lies in the interval with a given posterior probability, unlike a frequentist confidence interval
entries.locator: van de Schoot et al. (2021), Nature Reviews Methods Primers

entries.claim: MCMC methods such as Metropolis-Hastings, Gibbs sampling and NUTS draw samples from a posterior that has no closed form, and require convergence diagnostics
entries.locator: Stan documentation; PyMC documentation at https://www.pymc.io/

entries.claim: The posterior mean for the Beta-binomial model equals (alpha+h)/(alpha+beta+n); for Beta(62,42) this is about 0.596 with a 95 percent interval near [0.50, 0.69]
entries.notes: Elementary Beta moments and quantiles; interval quoted approximately
